The story

  • The fastball is one of one: 99.4 mph and 2544 rpm, 99th and 97th percentile; no other righty four-seam season in a Phillies game since 2015 sits at or above him on both.
  • The client's line reconciles exactly: .280 wOBA, .633 OPS, 26% K, 8.2% BB.
  • Lefties were the clean side (33.3% K, 1 walk); righties hit .179 but hard (41.9% HH).
  • The Bridge to Duran: 4 outings, all from 2026-08-31 on.
  • Down the stretch the heater came down a tick: four-seam 100.0 mph in his first 16 regular-season outings, 98.1 in the last 3 (sinker 99.4 → 98.0); 99.6 in the Wild Card. Descriptive, not graded.

Hand-in-hand

CommentaryTime to recap Alex McFarlane's 2026 season. Frankly, it has to go hand-in-hand with the guy who was drafted in the round following McFarlane back in 2022. A fellow right-handed college reliever from Florida, Orion Kerkering. Taken in the 5th round out of South Florida†, Kerk was rushed to the majors back in 2023 to pitch in leverage situations for several iterations of this ballclub.
The dataBoth 2022 draftees out of Florida colleges (McFarlane, 4th round, Miami; Kerkering, 5th, South Florida). Kerkering's first 21 MLB outings ran 2023-09-24 to 2024-05-13 and included 7 postseason games; McFarlane's ran 2026-07-22 to 2026-09-30 with 2. HP-11b corrects the school.

Stretch S-1: the first 21 outings

S-1 (posed by the org, built): through 21 MLB outings each, McFarlane .280 wOBA / .299 xwOBA, 25.9% K, 8.2% BB, 41.1% hard-hit, 99.4 mph four-seam; Kerkering .258 / .277, 23.5% K, 10.6% BB, 25.5% hard-hit, 97.6 mph. Kerkering arrived into October (7 of his first 21 were postseason); McFarlane arrived into a pennant race (2). McFarlane missed more bats and walked fewer; Kerkering allowed far softer contact.

The arrival

CommentaryNow it was Alex McFarlane's time to ascend to the big league bullpen. During the fateful weekend in Atlanta which cost Rob Thomson his job, Alex McFarlane sat in the Phillies bullpen. Ready to be used. He was not needed.
The dataRecalled from Double-A Reading on 4/24 before the Atlanta series; Thomson was dismissed 4/28 (carry-ins CI-1, CI-2). The log has no McFarlane pitch until 2026-07-22: he sat, and was not needed.
CommentaryMcFarlane dominated AA for most of 2026, I do not have statcast data for that. I do have data from his brief stint in AAA along with all 333 of his major league pitches across 21 outings including two postseason games.
The dataAAA is a supporting tier: 4 Lehigh Valley outings 2026-07-29 to 2026-08-08, 73 pitches, 8 K and 2 BB in 17 PA, 32% whiffs. Stints: MLB debut 2026-07-22 (12 pitches), AAA, then MLB from 2026-08-11 through the Wild Card. MLB evidence: 333 pitches, 21 outings (19 regular season + 2 Wild Card).

Bridge to Duran

CommentaryMcFarlane emerged as a key plank in the Bridge to Duran, the highwire act conducted by Don Mattingly when protecting a lead down the stretch for this ballclub. McFarlane's presence in the "Circle of Trust" belied his inexperience. His eye-popping stuff plays against big league hitters. Improved command in 2026 brought improved results with solid underlying metrics.
The dataBD-1: 4 of 19 regular-season outings came with a lead and Duran to follow, the first on 2026-08-31; he left with the lead intact in 3 of 4. He entered with the lead 9 times. 'Emerged … down the stretch' fits; 'key plank' is ahead of four outings (PARTLY). Command can't be compared to a prior year (no pre-2026 pitch data; NOT OBSERVABLE).

Overall year

CommentaryFirst we take a look at his overall year. He pitched to a .280 wOBA (good!) and .633 OPS (solid!). Decent chunk of hard hits and barrels, but very strong whiff in total and good chase. Pointing to quality stuff. 26% K and 8.2% BB are good. The ratio just exceeding 3:1 is quite good.
The dataExact: .280 wOBA, .633 OPS, 25.9% K, 8.2% BB, 22:7 K:BB. Against 258 Phillies pitcher-seasons since 2015 (regular season only): whiff 27.9% = 73rd pct, chase 31.7% = 74th, hard-hit 40.4% (pool median 35.7%). xwOBA .299 sits a touch above the .280 wOBA: results ran slightly ahead of contact quality.

Pitch plot

CommentaryThen we look at his pitch plot which is... hard to contextualize. Lots of FF that ride between 12 and 18 inches and run about 9 inches†. His sinker runs up to 18 inches. Bullet slider angles nicely off his FF which likely explains the deception to lefties. Speeds them up with heaters up and out over the plate. Follows that with a hammer slider that looks the same out of the hand before falling off the table. Sweeper sweeps at least a foot but is fairly flat, but can tunnel off his sinker when on.
The dataFF: 12.9–16.5 in of ride (10th–90th pct), 9.5 in of run (median). SI: 16.4 in of run, 18.6 in at the 90th pct. SL: 4.7 in sweep, -2.0 in IVB (bullet-adjacent: BS-1r draws the line at 4.0 / 4.0). ST: 12.9 in sweep, 2.3 in IVB. The log tags one slider (SL, 70 pitches, IVB -4.7 to 1.2 in): the 'bullet' and the 'hammer' are one pitch type here. FF to lefties: 42% upper third or above the zone. The Stuff-model subtitle is the client's read (no stuff model in the plane).

Outlier fastball

CommentaryWhich is indicating that he has an outlier fastball. So we build a graph to contextualize against other right-handed four-seam fastballs either thrown by Phillies pitchers or to Phillies batters since 2015. McFarlane has elite spin and elite velocity. His fastball is an outlier.
The dataFO-1: 99.4 mph (99th pct, #3 of 239 pitcher-seasons) and 2544 rpm (97th pct, #6). No other RHP four-seam season thrown in a Phillies game since 2015 (≥ 100 FF) sits at or above him on both. Pitch level: 0.3% of 137,203 righty four-seamers beat his average velocity and spin together.

Caveats

  • Small sample. 85 PA and 333 pitches; every stand × pitch cell is under 50 swings. Read rates as directional.
  • Client frame vs governed context. The client's tables include the 2 Wild Card games (as his `pps` does); context percentiles use his 313 regular-season pitches against regular-season pools.
  • One automatic ball (9/27, no pitch thrown) is inside the 333 and counts as in-zone in the inherited chase function (AB-1, D-7). It moves the vs-LHB usage shares to a 99.4% total; no headline moves.
  • FO-1 is raw velocity and spin, not drift-adjusted (UC #47 drift-adjusts; the order does not change at the top). Opponent pitchers in the pool are identified by MLBAM id only (EN-3: in batting rows `player_name` is the hitter).
  • AAA is a supporting tier (counts, usage, velocity, whiff), never blended into MLB rates; AA has no Statcast in the plane.
  • Carry-ins (draft, recalls, Thomson dismissal, AA line) are quoted from public sources and never computed on.
  • Postseason: 2 Wild Card outings vs Atlanta, 6 PA. Too few to read.
